title: Early Voting Starts! Americans Begin Choosing Congress for 2026
summary:
Imagine standing in line before the doors even open, just to be one of the first people to vote. That's what 18-year-old college student Sanya Singhal did Friday morning in Fairfax, Virginia. "Why not just have a little fun in life, you know, try to be the first early voter?" she said. "I really want to participate in my democracy."

Friday was the first day of in-person early voting for this year's midterm elections. That's a big vote that happens halfway through a president's four-year term. This time, it will decide which party controls Congress — the House and the Senate. The election is Nov. 3. Virginia started early voting Friday. In Idaho, Minnesota and South Dakota, people can now vote absentee in person, usually at a local election office. More states will open early voting in the coming weeks.

Why does it matter? If Democrats win back Congress, they could launch investigations into President Donald Trump's administration. If Republicans keep control, Trump's agenda is more likely to move forward. Voters are thinking about rising gas and grocery prices, the war in Iran, and artificial intelligence.

At a voting center near Richmond, a poll worker rang a bell as the building opened, and about a dozen people walked in. William Curry, a 74-year-old retiree, said he mostly approves of Trump's job — except for the war with Iran. "He's in a mess he can't get rid of," Curry said. In Sioux Falls, South Dakota, 67-year-old Bill Goehring voted for a mix of Democrats and independents. He said Trump's "dictatorial tendencies are bad for America." Election officials say they're ready and confident the vote will be accurate and secure.
why_it_matters: The people who win seats in Congress make rules that reach your school, your roads and your family's grocery bill — so days like this early-voting Friday are the first step in decisions that will affect you too.

background_read: Congress (the part of the U.S. government that makes the country's laws) has two parts — the House of Representatives and the Senate — and voters choose its members in elections held every two years.

Midterm elections come every four years, halfway through a president's four-year term, so President Donald Trump (the U.S. president since 2025) is not on the ballot even though the results will shape what he can do.

Voting before Election Day is not new — some states have allowed early or mail voting for decades, and it became much more common after the 2020 election, when many people wanted to avoid crowded polling places.

WHY: The result decides whether Democrats can launch investigations into President Donald Trump's administration or Republicans can push his agenda forward, with voters focused on prices, the war in Iran and artificial intelligence.
